subject.title: fix(agents): bound SSH directory uploads with a hard timeout

question: Should SSH sandbox uploads have a fixed process-wide maximum duration, or should timeout handling remain scoped to connection/handshake failure and caller-owned operation deadlines?
rationale: This changes an existing transfer from duration-bound behavior to a fixed failure policy, and the patch does not establish that the existing OpenSSH connection controls leave the stated handshake gap.

options.title: Narrow to the verified failure
options.body: Recommended: reproduce the real SSH failure first, then target only the unbounded connection or no-progress phase without killing valid long uploads.

options.title: Adopt a hard transfer limit
options.body: Keep a global deadline only after explicitly accepting that existing slow or large uploads may fail and documenting the supported override boundary.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Close or defer the PR if real OpenSSH behavior already bounds the reported handshake path and no separate hang is demonstrated.

recommendation.title: Narrow to the verified failure
recommendation.body: Recommended: reproduce the real SSH failure first, then target only the unbounded connection or no-progress phase without killing valid long uploads.

likelyOwner.reason: Best available low-confidence routing candidate for the agent-sandbox compatibility decision.
